# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Partner integration receives empty/unusable responses
**Description:** A partner's non-browser server-to-server integration received empty/unusable (non-API) responses when calling the CloudFront distribution, while the CloudFront 4xx graph stayed flat.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:30:00Z - 2026-10-10T19:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: TokenAbsentChallengeRule challenges tokenless partner client
**Description:** The Web ACL rule TokenAbsentChallengeRule (Priority 6) matches the label awswaf:managed:token:absent and issues a Challenge action. A non-browser server-to-server client cannot run the JavaScript silent challenge, so it never acquires a WAF token — every request trips this rule and receives an HTTP 202 interstitial (not a 4xx). This explains both the empty/unusable responses and the flat 4xx graph. Metrics (ChallengeRequests 1:1 with Requests) and WAF logs (599 Challenge/202 from a single IP, zero blocks) support this.
**Cascades to:** symptom-partner-empty-responses

#### Supporting Observations
- **Telemetry: 100% of requests challenged, 4xx flat at 0%:** In the incident window, WAFV2 ChallengeRequests for TokenAbsentChallengeRule matched CloudFront Requests 1:1 (89, 150, 150, 150, 60 per 5-min bucket) — every request was challenged. CloudFront 4xxErrorRate/5xxErrorRate/TotalErrorRate were flat at 0% throughout, and there were zero BlockedRequests. This is exactly why the partner saw empty/unusable (202 interstitial) responses while the 4xx graph looked healthy.
- **WAF logs: 599 Challenge/202 from TokenAbsentChallengeRule:** WAF logs for the window show 599 CHALLENGE requests, all with terminatingRuleId=TokenAbsentChallengeRule and responseCodeSent=202, all from a single source IP 198.51.100.50 (US). Zero BLOCK actions in the window.

### Root Cause: Web ACL mandates a browser-solvable WAF token with no exemption for the legitimate partner
**Description:** The steady-state design of example-bot-dev-web-acl issues a browser-only JavaScript Challenge (TokenAbsentChallengeRule, Priority 6) to ANY request carrying the awswaf:managed:token:absent label, with no exemption for the known legitimate acme-logistics server-to-server integration. A non-browser client (python-requests) can never obtain a WAF token, so it is challenged 100% of the time. CloudTrail confirms no config change triggered this (Terraform-provisioned ~2026-07-25) — the incident window is simply when the partner began calling. Fixing this (an IP/header exemption) is what stops the symptom recurring; the Challenge mechanism cascades from this design gap.
**Cascades to:** finding-token-challenge

#### Supporting Observations
- **WAF logs: 599 Challenge/202 from TokenAbsentChallengeRule:** WAF logs for the window show 599 CHALLENGE requests, all with terminatingRuleId=TokenAbsentChallengeRule and responseCodeSent=202, all from a single source IP 198.51.100.50 (US). Zero BLOCK actions in the window.
- **Telemetry: 100% of requests challenged, 4xx flat at 0%:** In the incident window, WAFV2 ChallengeRequests for TokenAbsentChallengeRule matched CloudFront Requests 1:1 (89, 150, 150, 150, 60 per 5-min bucket) — every request was challenged. CloudFront 4xxErrorRate/5xxErrorRate/TotalErrorRate were flat at 0% throughout, and there were zero BlockedRequests. This is exactly why the partner saw empty/unusable (202 interstitial) responses while the 4xx graph looked healthy.
- **No configuration change — steady-state behavior:** CloudTrail shows no mutative WAFV2 or CloudFront changes to example-bot-dev-web-acl, its IP sets, or distribution EEXAMPLE000002 on 2026-10-10 or in the prior 7 days. Only read-only GetWebACL at 18:59 UTC during the incident. The challenge behavior is pre-existing, not newly introduced.
- **Affected client identity & labels:** Single source IP 198.51.100.50 (US), UA python-requests/2.32.3, header x-partner-id: acme-logistics. All records carry label awswaf:managed:token:absent plus Bot Control signals (non_browser_user_agent, category:http_library, bot:name:python_requests) — all in COUNT mode, non-terminating. Confirms a legitimate non-browser partner integration, not an attack.

## Other Gaps

### Challenge (HTTP 202) responses are invisible on the CloudFront 4xx graph
**Description:** The WAF Challenge action returns HTTP 202 (success-class), so 100%-failing partner traffic never registered on CloudFront's 4xxErrorRate/5xxErrorRate/TotalErrorRate (all flat at 0.0%). There is currently no alarm or dashboard surfacing WAF ChallengeRequests, so this class of partner-impacting failure is a monitoring blind spot.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Add the partner acme-logistics source IP 198.51.100.50/32 to the existing allow IP set example-bot-dev-allowed-ips so AllowedIPsRule (Priority 2, Allow) exempts the partner before TokenAbsentChallengeRule (Priority 6, Challenge) runs

## Reasoning
The Web ACL challenges every request carrying awswaf:managed:token:absent. The partner's non-browser python-requests client can never obtain a WAF token, so all 599 requests received an HTTP 202 challenge and the integration is unusable. This is steady-state Terraform config (no rollback applies) and recurs on every partner call until exempted. Adding the partner /32 to the already-referenced allow IP set is the lowest-blast-radius fix: no rule changes, fully reversible. The allow IP set is currently empty. Trade-off: IP allow-listing trusts the entire source IP; a header+IP scope-down is more spoof-resistant and is captured as a durable code change.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Record the current Addresses array (expected empty []) as the rollback…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71
```
**Purpose:** Record the current Addresses array (expected empty []) as the rollback baseline before any modification.
**Advisory:** Capture the Addresses array exactly as returned; it is the authoritative rollback baseline.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Obtain the fresh LockToken immediately before the update to avoid an…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71 --query 'LockToken' --output text
```
**Purpose:** Obtain the fresh LockToken immediately before the update to avoid an optimistic-lock conflict.
**Advisory:** WAFv2 LockTokens change on every write; always use the token fetched immediately before the update.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Exempt the partner source IP from the token challenge by adding…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71 --addresses 198.51.100.50/32 --lock-token <LOCK_TOKEN_FROM_PRE_VALIDATE>
```
**Purpose:** Exempt the partner source IP from the token challenge by adding 198.51.100.50/32 to the allow IP set. Preserve any pre-existing addresses from the backup and append the partner /32.
**Risks:** All traffic from 198.51.100.50 bypasses the token challenge — this trusts the entire source IP, not just the partner application.
**Advisory:** On WAFOptimisticLockException, re-run the pre_validate get-ip-set for a fresh LockToken and retry., CLOUDFRONT-scope changes propagate globally and may take a short time across edge locations.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Verify the Addresses array now contains 198.51.100.50/32
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71 --query 'IPSet.Addresses' --output json
```
**Purpose:** Verify the Addresses array now contains 198.51.100.50/32.

#### 4.2 Verify end-to-end that the partner's non-browser access is restored and…
**Type:** text
Have acme-logistics retry a representative server-to-server request from 198.51.100.50 and confirm a normal HTTP 2xx application response instead of a 202 challenge. Optionally confirm TokenAbsentChallengeRule Challenge count for the partner drops to zero and AllowedIPsRule registers the traffic.
**Purpose:** Verify end-to-end that the partner's non-browser access is restored and the challenge no longer terminates its requests.
**Advisory:** WAF Challenge counts and CloudFront metrics may lag a few minutes; allow for propagation.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Fetch a fresh LockToken immediately before reverting
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71 --query 'LockToken' --output text
```
**Purpose:** Fetch a fresh LockToken immediately before reverting.

#### 5.2 Restore the backed-up prepare-phase baseline, removing the partner IP
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-bot-dev-allowed-ips --id 2efb85f7-5f0d-4473-b8df-eef754982a71 --addresses <BASELINE_ADDRESSES_FROM_PREPARE> --lock-token <FRESH_LOCK_TOKEN>
```
**Purpose:** Restore the backed-up prepare-phase baseline, removing the partner IP. If the baseline was empty, pass an empty list. Run only if partner traffic must be re-subjected to the challenge.
**Risks:** Reverting re-exposes acme-logistics to the token challenge, breaking its non-browser integration again.
**Advisory:** Restore exactly the baseline Addresses captured in prepare so no previously-trusted IPs are lost.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Persist the partner exemption in the Terraform-managed WAF config so it is not reverted as drift on the next terraform apply
**Description:** The Web ACL and its IP sets are Terraform-provisioned (~2026-07-25). Codify the exemption in the aws_wafv2_ip_set resource for example-bot-dev-allowed-ips (add 198.51.100.50/32). Preferably also add a scope-down to TokenAbsentChallengeRule that exempts trusted partner traffic matched by BOTH the x-partner-id: acme-logistics header AND the partner source IP, so a spoofed header alone cannot bypass the challenge. Document the owner so the entry is reviewed/removed when the integration changes.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Terraform state/plan show 198.51.100.50/32 (and any header-based scope-down, if adopted) as managed config, so terraform apply does not remove it.
- Requests from 198.51.100.50 bearing x-partner-id: acme-logistics receive normal application responses (not HTTP 202 challenges).
- All other tokenless non-browser clients continue to receive the Priority-6 challenge (protection unchanged).
- The exemption is documented with an owner and a review/expiry expectation.
